chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When there is a slave girl for one of you, whom he sleeps with, and then he frees her, and she observes her waiting period and marries, if she gives birth in five months, then the child is from her master who freed her; and if she gives birth after marrying in six months, then the child is for her later husband.
ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a freed slave girl who marries and gives birth within a short period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia legal principle of *Iradah* (presumption of paternity) applied to a *Umm al-Walad* (freed slave concubine) who marries after her master's emancipation. It establishes a specific chronological rule: if she gives birth within five months of the new marriage, the child is attributed to the former master who freed her; if birth occurs after six months, paternity is presumed to belong to the new husband. This distinction highlights the juristic focus on the duration of gestation to resolve lineage disputes in cases of sequential relationships.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When there was the slave girl for one of you, so he sleeps with her, and then frees her, so she observes the waiting period and marries. So if she gives birth in five months, so it would be from her master whom had freed her, and if she were to give birth after having married, in six months, so it would be for her later husband’.
